claim: fullWindowCount is assigned only inside the `if ts == ev.startTimestamp || selVS.Timestamp == nil` guard, so on @-modifier reuse steps (e.g. predict_linear(x[60s] @ 30, 3600) over a range) it stays 0 and IncrementSamplesAtStep adds nothing; the pre-change code counted the retained full window unconditionally. This regresses TotalSamples / prometheus_engine_query_samples_total / totalQueryableSamplesPerStep (measured 16 -> 4, per-step [4,4,4,4] -> [4,0,0,0]) despite the change's comment and doc claiming those semantics are unchanged.
raw: #1 High: `@`-modifier reuse path silently stops incrementing `TotalSamples` — an existing metric and API field regress

claim: evalSubquery now merges the child's SamplesRead into the parent via MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery, but the subquery output is then re-counted by IncrementSamplesReadAtStep in the matrixIterSlice step loop (line 2184), so f(subquery) is counted twice (measured max_over_time(metricWith3SampleEvery10Seconds[60s:5s]) gives TotalSamples=36, SamplesRead=72; bare subquery is not doubled). This contradicts the docs (api.md:247, feature_flags.md:48, query_stats.go:279-281) claiming SamplesRead equals totalQueryableSamples for non-subquery cases, inflates prometheus_engine_query_samples_read_total, and the new tests encode the doubling as expected.
raw: #2 High: `SamplesRead` double counts every subquery used as a range-vector function argument, contradicting its own documentation

claim: countSamplesAfter linearly scans the entire retained floats/histograms window at every step of every series (called from engine.go:2164), replacing an O(1) len(floats), and runs unconditionally since engine counters are always accumulated. Measured BenchmarkRangeQuery rate(a_one[1d]),steps=1000: ~7.17ms/op base -> ~9.8-11.0ms/op head (+38%), changes(a_one[1d]) +14%. Since the buffer is sorted ascending, a backward scan or binary search (or having matrixIterSlice return the appended count) would be O(new points).
raw: #3 High: `countSamplesAfter` adds an O(window) scan per step per series to the hottest engine loop — ~38% slowdown measured on wide-window range queries
